back: The economic problem arising because wants are unlimited while the resources available to satisfy them are limited.
The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made.
What to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce.

front: What is the difference between **scarcity** and a **shortage**?
back: Scarcity is permanent and applies to all economic goods; a shortage is when demand exceeds supply at the current price.
A good that is scarce and has an opportunity cost, so it must be produced and normally has a price.
A good with no opportunity cost because it is available in such abundance that using more does not reduce what others can have.

front: A farmer's options earn US\$900, US\$500 and US\$300. She picks the US\$900 option. What is the opportunity cost?
back: US\$500, the next best alternative; not the sum of the other two.

front: Why is a free school meal not free to society?
back: It uses scarce resources (food, labour, fuel) that have alternative uses.
Individuals (income and time), firms (inputs) and governments (tax revenue).
